questions.title: The bony structure protecting the brain
questions.question: Which of the following bony structures protects the brain?

explanations.A: Incorrect. The sternum, together with the rib cage, protects the heart and great vessels in the thorax, not the brain.
explanations.B: Correct. The cranium (neurocranium) is the bony vault — built from the occipital, sphenoid, ethmoid and frontal bones plus the paired parietal and temporal bones — that encloses and protects the brain. It is joined at immobile sutures once growth is complete, giving the brain a rigid protective case. Each of the body's other major organs has its own dedicated bony guard: the heart has the sternum and rib cage, the spinal cord the vertebral column, and the pelvic viscera the bony pelvis.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The pelvis protects the pelvic viscera (bladder, rectum, and reproductive organs), not the brain.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The rib cage protects the lungs and, anteriorly with the sternum, the heart — it plays no role in protecting the brain.

questions.learning_objective: Name the cranium as the bone protecting the brain, distinct from the sternum/ribs (heart/lungs) and pelvis (pelvic viscera).
